thread.title: Call me Debbie Downer but as the weeks pass with percentage

author: Income Machine
title: Call me Debbie Downer but as the weeks pass with percentage
text:
Call me Debbie Downer but as the weeks pass with percentage point gains across the indexes, I become more and more disgruntled. I’m absolutely cranky. There is so much cheerleading that many of us have lost sight of just how overvalued this market has become. One of the most basic points of reference is the Shiller PE Ratio which is accelerating toward its all-time high reached during the dot-com bubble:

I get it. Corporate tax reform will boost EPS. The reduction in individual rates will provide consumers with more dollars to spend on goods and services. Companies like Apple ( AAPL ) are sitting on mountains of cash and will repatriate offshore money at a sweetheart rate. The labor participation rate is soaring. Debt remains historically cheap and the unemployment rate is getting so low it may meet the 30-year Treasury yield. GDP is revised upward each month and the Federal Reserve may raise rates as many as four times next year to control inflation.
It’s enough good news to put a bear in hibernation. The factors above are overwhelmingly positive but investors are gobbling up shares as if the news is not priced in.
It is, and then some.
If the Dow Jones (DJIA) was at 17,000 instead of nearly 26,000, I’d pick up my pom-poms and cheer along too, but it’s not. Take a look at the 10-year chart of the Dow to see its rapid ascent past bubble territory:
